root.label: Futures, promises and async
root.note: Providers and futures share one state that carries exactly one value or exception between threads.

children.label: Shared state
children.note: Holds a value or exception, a ready flag, and possibly a deferred function.

children.label: Providers
children.note: promise, packaged_task and std::async write the result into the state.

children.label: Return objects
children.note: future and shared_future read the result; the last reference destroys the state.

children.label: Synchronization
children.note: Making the state ready synchronizes with the wait or get that observes it.

children.label: promise and future
children.note: A one-shot pipe: one get_future, one result, one get.

children.label: broken_promise
children.note: A provider destroyed without a result stores this error, so get throws instead of hanging.

children.label: Single-use errors
children.note: future_already_retrieved for a second get_future; promise_already_satisfied for a second result.

children.label: get moves out
children.note: future<T>::get moves the value and releases the state; valid() is then false.

children.label: Invalid future
children.note: Using a future with valid() false is undefined; throwing no_state is only recommended.

children.label: At thread exit
children.note: set_value_at_thread_exit makes the state ready after thread_local objects are destroyed.

children.label: shared_future
children.note: Copyable view of the state for many consumers, made by future::share().

children.label: Repeatable get
children.note: get returns const T& and leaves the value in place; every get rethrows a stored exception.

children.label: One copy per thread
children.note: Give each thread its own shared_future object rather than sharing one.

children.label: packaged_task
children.note: A move-only callable that stores its result or exception in a shared state.

children.label: Run once
children.note: A second call throws promise_already_satisfied.

children.label: reset
children.note: Abandons the old state and creates a fresh one, which needs a new future.

children.label: std::async
children.note: Decay-copies arguments and returns a future for the function's result.

children.label: launch::async
children.note: Runs as if on a new thread; throws system_error if no thread can be started.

children.label: launch::deferred
children.note: Runs lazily in the thread that first calls get or wait; never if nobody asks.

children.label: Default policy
children.note: async | deferred lets the implementation choose; timed waits may return deferred forever.

children.label: Blocking destructor
children.note: The last future for a launched async state waits for the task, so discarded results serialize.

children.label: No continuations
children.note: Standard futures can only be blocked on or polled, never chained.

children.label: Concurrency TS
children.note: future::then, when_all and when_any stayed in std::experimental and were not adopted.

children.label: C++26 senders
children.note: std::execution composes work lazily with schedulers; see senders-and-receivers.
